column1: # Android is Kotlin and the backend is TypeScript, so the code is not shared.
# This file is. Both sides read THIS file and must produce the same numbers:
# A fixture added here is run by both automatically — neither side can quietly
# drift, and neither can pass by keeping its own private copy of the numbers.
# Format: tab-separated. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.
#   field 1  label (what the case is about, in words)
# Inputs use ";" between entries and ":" inside one entry. "-" means "empty".
#   money    integer poisha        1 BDT = 100 poisha, so 50 BDT = 5000
#   quantity integer scaled x1000  1 piece = 1000, 0.5 kg = 500
# The division is where a line total can land between two poisha. It is
# resolved by rounding half AWAY FROM ZERO, so that reversing a line gives
# back exactly what the line charged (see the paired +/- 1.25 kg cases below).
